  "text": "The harbor steps were slick with weed. At the bottom, where the tide should have been falling, water pressed against the stone without a ripple.

Mara’s sister gripped the rail. “I let go,” she said.

“You were little,” their mother told her.

“I know. I still let go.”

The child went down ahead of them, carrying the spoon. At the last step she crouched and held it out over the water. A drop fell from its bowl. It struck the surface with a sound like a knock on a door.

Far beneath them, someone knocked back.

Mara took the rope from her coat pocket. She had brought it without remembering why, though her hands smelled of salt. One end was frayed; the other bore a knot her father had taught them to tie.

She fastened it to the rail. Her sister caught the loose end and lowered it into the water. They waited. The rope drifted sideways, then drew taut.

Their mother made a sound in her throat. Mara leaned over the rail, but saw only her own face and a pale shape moving below it.

The child lifted the spoon again. “The steps,” she called. “Come to the steps.”

The water began to recede. It slipped down one stone, then another, leaving a line of shells along the edge. Beneath the harbor wall, a narrow passage appeared, its floor shining wetly. The rope led into the dark.

Mara’s sister tested the knot, then put one foot on the exposed step. This time, Mara held her sleeve."
